q: Under RA 9266, Section 31, how is the act of soliciting architectural work by a non-registered and unlicensed person characterized?
o: As a purely civil matter with no penal consequence
As offering to practice architecture, which is unlawful for non-registered and unlicensed persons to do
As lawful so long as no contract is actually signed
As permissible marketing activity distinct from practice
Study first pa muna po
n: Section 31 states "solicitation of architectural work shall be construed as offering to practice architecture and shall be unlawful for any non-registered and unlicensed persons to do so." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 31)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 26 (Vested Rights), what happens to architects who were already registered at the time the law took effect?
o: They must retake the licensure examination under the new subjects
Their prior registrations are voided and they must reapply from scratch

They are automatically registered under the provisions of the new Act, subject to future requirements, and their existing Certificates of Registration in good standing have the same force and effect as if issued after the Act's passage
They must pay a one-time transition fee equal to double the usual registration fee
n: Section 26 provides all previously registered architects "shall automatically be registered under the provisions hereof, subject...to the provisions herein set forth as to future requirements," and their certificates "shall have the same force and effect as though issued after the passage of this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 26)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 12, the licensure examination for architects is given by the Board in places and dates designated by the Commission, in accordance with which other law?
o: Republic Act No. 7160
Republic Act No. 8981
Republic Act No. 1581
Republic Act No. 545
n: Section 12 requires the examination to be given "in such places and dates as the Commission may designate in accordance with the provisions of Republic Act No. 8981." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 12)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 23(b), it is a ground for suspension or revocation of a Certificate of Registration if an architect:
o: Has hired more than five employees in his firm
Has paid money, except the regular fees provided for, to secure a Certificate of Registration
Has practiced architecture for more than 20 years
Has attended more CPD seminars than required
n: Section 23(b) names as a ground "has paid money except the regular fees provided for to secure a Certificate of Registration." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(b))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 8, who has custody of all records of the Board, including applications for examination and administrative/investigative case records, and who designates the Secretary of the Board?
o: The Department of Trade and Industry
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization
The local government unit where the Board sits
The Professional Regulation Commission
n: Section 8 provides that "all records of the Board...shall be under the custody of the Commission," and "the Commission shall designate the Secretary of the Board." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 8)

q: Which term under RA 9266 refers to the architect who is directly and professionally responsible and liable specifically for the construction supervision of a project?
o: Architect-of-record
Architecture-in-charge of construction
General Practice architect
Consulting Architect
n: Section 3(2)(b) defines "Architecture-in-charge of construction" as an architect "directly and professionally responsible and liable for the construction supervision of the project." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(2)(b))

q: Section 7(l) of RA 9266 requires the Board, in coordination with which agency, to ensure that higher educational instruction and offerings of architecture comply with prescribed policies, standards and requirements in curriculum, faculty, library and facilities?
o: The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
The Commission on Higher Education (CHED)
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)
n: Section 7(l) empowers the Board, "in coordination with the CHED," to ensure architecture education complies with CHED's policies, standards and requirements on curriculum, faculty, library and facilities. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(l))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 18, the Certificate of Registration issued to a passing examinee shall bear the signature of:
o: Only the president of the integrated and accredited professional organization
Only the examinee's college dean
The chairperson of the Commission and the chairman and members of the Board, stamped with the official seal
Only the Secretary of Justice
n: Section 18 states the Certificate of Registration "shall bear the signature of the chairperson of the Commission and the chairman and members of the Board, stamped with the official seal." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 18)

q: Structurally, how is RA 9266 organized, and which Article deals specifically with examination, registration and licensure of architects?
o: It has five Articles; Article III covers Examination, Registration and Licensure (Sections 12-28)
It has a single Article covering all subject matter without subdivision
It has seven Articles; Article V covers examination matters
It has three Articles; Article II covers examination matters
n: RA 9266 is organized into five Articles: Article I (General Provision), Article II (Professional Regulatory Board), Article III (Examination, Registration and Licensure, Sections 12-28), Article IV (Practice of Architecture, Sections 29-39), and Article V (Final Provisions, Sections 40-47). (Source: RA 9266, Table of Articles)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 39, the implementing rules and regulations for the professional liability insurance requirement for foreign nationals practicing under a temporary/special permit shall be implemented by the Board, in consultation with the integrated and accredited professional organization, within how many months from the effectivity of the Act?
o: Two (2) years
One (1) year
Three (3) months
Six (6) months
n: Section 39 provides these rules "shall be implemented by the Board in consultation with the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects within six (6) months from the effectivity of this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 39)

q: Under Section 5(e) of RA 9266, which of the following is required of a person to qualify as a member of the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture?
o: He/she has never been convicted of any crime involving moral turpitude
He/she must have served as Board Secretary for at least two years
He/she must hold a foreign architecture license
He/she must be under 40 years of age
n: Section 5(e) requires that the prospective Board member "has never been convicted of any crime involving moral turpitude." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 5(e))

q: Under Section 20(5) of RA 9266, all architectural plans, designs, specifications, drawings and documents relative to the construction of a building shall bear the seal and signature of whom, along with what identifying details?
o: Only an architect registered and licensed under this Act, together with his/her professional identification card number and its expiration date
The local government building official, together with the permit control number
The building owner, together with the owner's taxpayer identification number
Any licensed engineer, together with the project's tax declaration number
n: Section 20(5) requires that such documents "bear the seal and signature only of an architect registered and licensed under this Act together with his/her professional identification card number and the date of its expiration." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(5))

q: Under Section 23(d) of RA 9266, which act is grounds for suspension or revocation of a Certificate of Registration?
o: Having taken a leave of absence from active practice for one year
Having relocated one's practice to another region of the country
Having declined to join the integrated professional organization's optional committees
Having aided or abetted in the practice of architecture any person not duly authorized to practice architecture in the Philippines
n: Section 23(d) lists as a ground for suspension or revocation that the registrant "has aided or abetted in the practice of architecture any person not duly authorized to practice architecture in the Philippines." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(d))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 33, drawings, specifications and other contract documents duly signed, stamped or sealed, as instruments of service, are treated as:
o: The intellectual property and documents of the architect, regardless of whether the object for which they are made is executed or not
Public records open to unrestricted copying
Property of the client immediately upon payment of the down payment
Property of the government upon issuance of a building permit
n: Section 33 provides such documents "are the intellectual property and documents of the architect, whether the object for which they are made is executed or not," and prohibits unauthorized duplication without the architect's written consent. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33)

q: Under Section 14(1) of RA 9266, which subject is expressly named as covered by the architecture licensure examination?
o: Environmental Science and Chemistry
Comparative Religion and World History
History and Theory of Architecture; Principles of Planning and Architectural Practice
Business Law and Taxation
n: Section 14(1) lists "History and Theory of Architecture; Principles of Planning and Architectural Practice" as one of the subjects covered by the licensure examination. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14(1))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 39, foreign nationals (including former Filipinos) wanting to engage in the general practice of architecture must locally secure what, commensurate with the nature and magnitude of their project involvement and compensation?
o: A life insurance policy payable to the Commission
A performance bond issued by the local government unit only
A cash deposit with the Bureau of Internal Revenue
Professional liability insurance or malpractice insurance, or an acceptable equivalent in bond form
n: Section 39 requires such foreign nationals to "secure locally their professional liability insurance or malpractice insurance or their acceptable equivalent in bond form commensurate with the nature and magnitude of their project involvement and their compensation." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 39)

q: A foreign architect enters the Philippines to perform professional services on a foreign-funded government project. Under RA 9266, Section 38, what must this foreign national secure before assuming duties as an architect or consultant on the project?
o: Nothing, since foreign-funded projects are exempt from RA 9266
Only a work visa from the Bureau of Immigration, with no PRC involvement
Only a certificate from his home country's embassy
A special/temporary permit from the Board, subject to approval of the Commission
n: Section 38 requires foreign nationals performing such services to, "before assuming the duties, functions and responsibilities as architects or consultants, secure a special/temporary permit from the Board subject to approval of the Commission." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 31, if a firm seeks to avoid the provisions of the Act by having an unregistered representative or employee seek architectural work on its behalf, what is the effect?
o: Only the unregistered representative is held liable, not the firm
Both the party represented and the representative — the employer and the employee — shall be deemed guilty of violation of this Act
No liability attaches unless actual construction work is completed
The firm is merely fined administratively with no criminal liability
n: Section 31 provides that in such a scheme, "both those represented and representative, the employer and the employee shall be deemed guilty of violation of this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 31)

q: An architecture professor wishes to be appointed to the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture. Under RA 9266, Section 5(d), what must a former faculty member of a school, institute, university or review center teaching architecture do before qualifying for Board membership?
o: Obtain a waiver signed by the school president
Officially resign from the institution and completely stop teaching, advising or reviewing activities for at least five (5) years prior to the nomination
Merely reduce teaching load by half for one year
Nothing — faculty members are automatically qualified
n: Section 5(d) disqualifies faculty members from Board membership "unless he/she had officially resigned from such an institution and has completely stopped teaching, advising or reviewing activities for at least five (5) years prior to the nomination." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 5(d))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 20(1), architectural plans and specifications prepared by, or under the direct supervision of, a registered architect shall be stamped with the architect's seal for how long?
o: Only until the building permit is approved
During the life of the registrant's certificate
Indefinitely, even after the certificate has been revoked
Only for one (1) year after issuance of the seal
n: Section 20(1) provides plans "shall be stampede [stamped] with said seal during the life of the registrant's certificate," and makes it unlawful to use the seal after the certificate has expired or been revoked unless renewed or reissued. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(1))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 38(c), foreign nationals granted a temporary/special permit shall be required to work with:
o: Only representatives of the foreign embassy
Only members of their own foreign firm
A Filipino counterpart, and shall also be responsible for public utilities and taxes due to the Philippine government relative to their participation in the project
No local counterpart at all
n: Section 38(c) requires "that foreign nationals shall be required to work with a Filipino counterpart and shall also be responsible for public utilities and taxes due to the Philippine government, relative to their participation in, or professional services rendered to the project." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38(c))

q: Under Section 9(c) of RA 9266, what event constitutes a ground for the President to suspend or remove a Board member?
o: Attendance at an international architecture conference
Voluntary resignation from the integrated professional organization
Final judgment of crimes involving moral turpitude
Publication of a scholarly article critical of the Board
n: Section 9(c) lists "final judgment of crimes involving moral turpitude" as a ground for suspension or removal of a Board member. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 9(c))

q: Under Section 14(2) of RA 9266, which examination subject covers structural design and building materials?
o: Structural Design, Building Materials, and Architectural Specifications, and Methods of Construction and Utilities
Urban Design and Architectural Interiors
History and Theory of Architecture
Architectural Design and Site Planning
n: Section 14(2) lists "Structural Design, Building Materials, and Architectural Specifications, and Methods of Construction and Utilities" as one of the examination subjects. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14(2))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 16, within how many calendar days after the licensure examination must the Board submit to the Commission the ratings obtained by each candidate, unless extended for just cause?
o: Sixty (60) calendar days
Twenty (20) calendar days
Thirty (30) calendar days
Fifteen (15) calendar days
n: Section 16 requires the Board to submit ratings "within thirty (30) calendar days after the examination, unless extended for just cause." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 16)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 22, may registration be refused, or a name removed from the roster of architects, solely on conviction for a purely political offense?
o: Yes, any criminal conviction whatsoever automatically bars registration
No, because Section 22 applies only to foreign nationals

No — the proviso in Section 22 states registration shall not be refused, nor a name removed from the roster, on conviction for a political offense or an offense that should not disqualify the person in the Board's opinion
Yes, but only if the conviction happened after registration
n: Section 22 provides "that registration shall not be refused and a name shall not be removed from the roster of architects on conviction for a political offense or for an offense which should not, in the opinion of the Board...disqualify a person from practicing under this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 22)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 32, it is unlawful for any architect to sign his/her name or affix his/her seal on plans made under another architect's supervision unless the signature clearly indicates:
o: The signing architect's Board examination score
The signing architect's home address
The part or parts of such work actually performed by the former (the signing architect)
The name of the client only
n: Section 32 requires that any such signature be made "in such manner as to clearly indicate the part or parts of such work actually performed by the former." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 32)

q: Section 5(b) of RA 9266 requires a Board member to hold what educational credential?
o: A degree in Bachelor of Science in Architecture conferred by a school, college or university recognized and/or accredited by the Commission on Higher Education (CHED)
A master's degree in business administration
A doctorate in civil engineering
A vocational certificate in drafting
n: Section 5(b) requires a Board member to "be a holder of a degree in Bachelor of Science in Architecture conferred by a school, college or university in the Philippines or abroad that is recognized and/or accredited by the Commission on Higher Education (CHED)." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 5(b))

q: Section 3(4)(i) of RA 9266 describes the scope of the practice of architecture as covering all works related to what overarching purpose?
o: The exclusive marketing and advertisement of construction materials
The financial auditing of construction companies

The scientific, aesthetic and orderly coordination of all works and branches necessary for the production of a complete building or structure, in order to enhance and safeguard life, health and property and promote the quality of life
The licensing of civil engineers and other allied professionals
n: Section 3(4)(i) covers "all works which relate to the scientific, aesthetic and orderly coordination of all works and branches of the work, systems and process necessary for the production of a complete building or structure...in order to enhance and safeguard life, health and property and the promotion and enrichment of the quality of life." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(i))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 41, the implementing rules and regulations shall themselves take effect how many days following their publication in the Official Gazette or in two major daily newspapers of general circulation?
o: Fifteen (15) days
Sixty (60) days
Thirty (30) days
Ten (10) days
n: Section 41 states the IRR "shall be effective fifteen (15) days following their publication in the Official Gazette or in two (2) major daily newspapers of general circulation." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 41)

q: An applicant for the architecture licensure examination holds a Bachelor of Science in Architecture degree and a Master's Degree in Architecture from a government-recognized institution, but has only one (1) year of actual diversified architectural experience. Under RA 9266, Section 13(c), is this applicant qualified to sit for the examination?
o: No, a Master's Degree disqualifies an applicant from taking the licensure examination

Yes — Section 13(c) credits one (1) year of practical experience to an applicant holding a recognized Master's Degree in Architecture, satisfying the two-year requirement when combined with the one (1) actual year
No, because two (2) years of actual diversified experience is required with no possible credit
Yes, but only if the applicant is over 30 years of age
n: Section 13(c) requires two (2) years of diversified experience but provides "an applicant holding a Master's Degree in Architecture from a school, college, university or institute recognized by the government shall be credited one (1) year in his/her practical experience," so one actual year plus the one-year credit satisfies the requirement. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13(c))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 35, within how many years from the effectivity of the Act must all existing and proposed government positions primarily requiring the services of an architect be filled only by registered and licensed architects?
o: Three (3) years
Five (5) years
One (1) year
Ten (10) years
n: Section 35 provides that "within (3) years from the effectivity of this Act, all existing and proposed positions in the local and national government...primarily requiring the services of an architect shall be filled only by registered and licensed architects." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 35)

q: A private developer compels a registered architect to perform general practice of architecture services for a project without first executing a written contract or service agreement. Under RA 9266, Section 30, upon conviction, this developer shall be sentenced to a fine of not less than how much, or imprisonment not exceeding how many years, or both?
o: No fine, only imprisonment not exceeding one (1) year
Not less than P1,000,000.00, imprisonment not exceeding ten (10) years
Not less than P200,000.00, imprisonment not exceeding six (6) years
Not less than P50,000.00, imprisonment not exceeding three (3) years
n: Section 30 penalizes any person or entity that forces an architect to perform services "without first executing a written contract/service agreement" with "a fine of not less than Two hundred thousand pesos (P200,000.00) or...imprisonment for a period not exceeding six (6) years, or both." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 30)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 18, what does the Professional Identification Card indicate, aside from being duly signed by the chairperson of the Commission?
o: The examinee's home address only
The examinee's college grade point average
The names of all Board members at the time of examination
The registration number, date of issuance, and expiry date
n: Section 18 provides that the Professional Identification Card bears "the registration number, date of issuance, expiry date, duly signed by the chairperson of the Commission." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 18)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 46 (Repealing Clause), which prior law is expressly repealed by RA 9266?
o: Republic Act No. 1581, standing alone
Republic Act No. 545, as amended by Republic Act No. 1581, otherwise known as "An Act to Regulate the Practice of Architecture in the Philippines"
Republic Act No. 8981, the PRC Modernization Act
Presidential Decree No. 1096, the National Building Code
n: Section 46 provides "Republic Act No. 545, as amended by Republic Act No. 1581 is hereby repealed," and the Act's title also identifies RA 545 as "An Act to Regulate the Practice of Architecture in the Philippines." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 46 (see also the Act's title))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 13, which of the following is NOT one of the stated qualifications for an applicant for the architecture licensure examination?
o: Being of good moral character
Not having been convicted of any criminal offense involving moral turpitude
Being a Filipino citizen or a qualified foreign citizen as provided in the Act
Holding a Master's Degree in Architecture as a mandatory minimum requirement
n: Section 13 requires a Bachelor of Science in Architecture degree plus diversified experience (with a Master's Degree merely crediting one year of experience) — a Master's Degree is not itself a mandatory qualification. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 4, Board members are appointed by the President from a list of how many recommendees, chosen from a list of how many nominees for each position submitted by the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects?
o: 1 recommendee chosen from 3 nominees
3 recommendees chosen from 5 nominees
2 recommendees chosen from 4 nominees
5 recommendees chosen from 10 nominees
n: Section 4 provides for appointment "from a lists of three (3) recommendees chosen from a list of five (5) nominees for each position submitted to the Commission by the integrated and the accredited professional organization of architects." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 4)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 40, once an architect is duly registered with the Board, what happens to his/her membership in the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects?
o: Membership is entirely voluntary and separate from registration
Membership requires a separate licensure examination
The architect shall automatically become a member upon payment of required fees and dues, and this does not bar membership in other associations of architects
Membership is only open to architects who graduated with honors
n: Section 40 provides a registered architect "shall automatically become member of the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects...upon payment of the required fees and dues," and that such membership "shall not be a bar to membership in other associations of architects." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 40)

q: Which of the following is explicitly listed under Section 3(4) of RA 9266 as part of the Scope of the Practice of Architecture?
o: Adjudication of labor disputes on construction sites
Preparation of preliminary, technical, economic and financial feasibility studies of plans, models and project promotional services
Issuance of building occupancy tax assessments
Certification of land titles
n: Section 3(4)(d) includes "preparation of preliminary, technical, economic and financial feasibility studies of plans, models and project promotional services" within the scope of the practice of architecture. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(d))

q: A foreign national who is not authorized to practice architecture in the Philippines stays in the country and performs activities described in Sections 3 and 4 of RA 9266 in connection with a building's construction. Under Section 25, how is this characterized?
o: As a lawful courtesy practice permitted to all foreign professionals
As acceptable so long as the foreign national is merely observing construction
As a form of consulting exempt from registration requirements
As engaging in the unauthorized practice of architecture
n: Section 25 provides that a foreign architect or unauthorized person performing such activities "shall be deemed engaged in the unauthorized practice of architecture." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 25)

q: Under Section 7(k) of RA 9266, the Board has the power to approve, issue, limit or cancel what type of authorization?
o: Passports for architects traveling abroad
Temporary or special permit to practice architecture
Import permits for construction equipment
Business licenses for hardware stores
n: Section 7(k) empowers the Board to "approve, issue, limit or cancel temporary or special permit to practice architecture." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(k))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 41, within how many days after the effectivity of the Act must the Board, subject to Commission approval and in coordination with the integrated and accredited professional organization, adopt and promulgate the implementing rules and regulations and the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice?
o: Ninety (90) days
Sixty (60) days
Fifteen (15) days
Thirty (30) days
n: Section 41 requires the Board, "within sixty (60) days after the effectivity of this Act," to adopt and promulgate the implementing rules and regulations and the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 41)

q: A foreign national seeking a temporary/special permit under Section 38 of RA 9266 must satisfy the condition in Section 38(b) that he/she is:
o: Sponsored by at least three Filipino architects
Legally qualified to practice architecture in his/her own country, and that his/her expertise is necessary and advantageous to the Philippines particularly in technology transfer and specialization
Exempt from all Philippine taxes during the permit period
A permanent resident of the Philippines for at least five years
n: Section 38(b) requires "that he/she is legally qualified to practice architecture in his/her own country, and that his/her expertise is necessary and advantageous to our country particularly in the aspects of technology transfer and specialization." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38(b))

q: Under Section 9(a) of RA 9266, which of the following is a ground for the President to suspend or remove a member of the Board?
o: Being a member of a review center faculty
Neglect of duty or incompetence
Being reappointed for a second term
Filing an annual report with the Commission
n: Section 9(a) lists "neglect of duty or incompetence" as a ground for the President, on the Commission's recommendation, to suspend or remove a Board member. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 9(a))

q: Under Section 3(4)(h) of RA 9266, which of the following is expressly listed as part of the scope of the practice of architecture?
o: Building programming, building administration, construction arbitration and architectural conservation and restoration
Land surveying and geodetic engineering
Issuance of occupancy permits by local government units
Sanitary and mechanical engineering design exclusively
n: Section 3(4)(h) lists "building programming, building administration, construction arbitration and architectural conservation and restoration" as part of the scope of the practice of architecture. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(h))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 29, aside from a fine, a person convicted of unauthorized practice of architecture may also suffer imprisonment for what range of time, at the discretion of the court?
o: Not less than six (6) months or not exceeding six (6) years
Life imprisonment
Not less than one (1) year or not exceeding two (2) years
A mandatory flat term of exactly one (1) year
n: Section 29 provides for "imprisonment for a period not less than six (6) months or not exceeding six (6) years, or both, at the discretion of the Court." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 40, the Architecture profession shall be integrated into one national organization accredited by the Board and approved by the Commission, which organization must in turn be registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as what kind of entity?
o: A for-profit stock corporation owned by the Board
A sole proprietorship owned by the Commission chairperson
A non-profit, non-stock corporation governed by by-laws providing for democratic election of its officials
A government-owned and controlled corporation
n: Section 40 requires the integrated organization to be "registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, as a non-profit, non-stock corporation to [be] governed by by-laws providing for a democratic election of its officials." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 40)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 45 (Separability Clause), if a clause, provision, paragraph or part of the Act is declared unconstitutional or invalid, what is the effect on the remainder of the Act?
o: The entire Act is automatically voided
The judgment shall not affect, invalidate or impair any other part of the Act; it is confined to the clause, provision, paragraph or part directly involved in the controversy
Only the remaining provisions of the same Article are voided
The Act must be re-enacted in its entirety by Congress
n: Section 45 provides such a judgment "shall not affect, invalidate or impair any other part hereof, but such judgment shall be merely confined to the clause, provision, paragraph or part directly involved in the controversy." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 45)

q: RA 9266 is described as a consolidation of which two bills, finally passed by the House of Representatives and the Senate on January 28, 2004 and January 29, 2004, respectively?
o: House Bill No. 9266 and Senate Bill No. 545
House Bill No. 2710 and Senate Bill No. 5389
House Bill No. 1096 and Senate Bill No. 8981
House Bill No. 5389 and Senate Bill No. 2710
n: The Act states: "This Act which is a consolidation of House Bill No. 5389 and Senate Bill No. 2710 was finally passed by the House of Representatives and the Senate on January 28 2004 and January 29, 2004, respectively." (Source: RA 9266, Enrolled Bill Notation)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 22, the Board shall refuse to register and issue a Certificate of Registration to a person who, among other grounds, is:
o: A person of unsound mind, or one convicted of a criminal offense involving moral turpitude, or one guilty of immoral and dishonorable conduct
A person who scored exactly 70% in the licensure examination
Simply younger than 25 years of age
A person who studied architecture abroad
n: Section 22 bars issuance of the certificate to persons who "falsely sworn or misrepresented" themselves, those "convicted by a court of competent jurisdiction of a criminal offense involving moral turpitude or guilty of immoral and dishonorable conduct," or "any person of unsound mind." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 22)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 3(11), all registered Filipino architects are, without prejudice to membership in other voluntary professional associations, members of what body?
o: The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of architects
The Department of Trade and Industry
The Securities and Exchange Commission
The Professional Regulation Commission's board of directors
n: Section 3(11) defines the "Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization" as "the existing official national organization of all architects of the Philippines in which all registered Filipino architects shall be members without prejudice to membership in other voluntary professional associations." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(11))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 44, who shall act as legal adviser to the Commission and the Board and render legal assistance in carrying out the provisions of the Act?
o: Any private law firm hired by the Board
The Secretary of Trade and Industry
The Secretary of Justice or his duly designated representative
The president of the integrated professional organization
n: Section 44 provides that "the Secretary of Justice or his duly designated representative shall act as legal adviser to the Commission and the Board and shall render legal assistance as may be necessary." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 44)

q: A project owner engages an architect who signs and seals the plans, specifications and contract documents and assumes civil liability for the total design of the project. Under RA 9266, what is this architect called?
o: Consulting Architect
Authorship architect
Architecture-in-charge of construction
Architect-of-record
n: Section 3(2)(a) defines the "Architect-of-record" as the architect "directly and professionally responsible for the total design of the project for the client and who shall assume the civil liability for the plans, specifications and contract documents he/she has signed and sealed." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(2)(a))

q: Under Section 37(c) of RA 9266, when a firm, partnership, association or corporation is registered for the practice of architecture, its individual members are responsible for what?
o: Their individual and collective acts as an entity and as provided by law
Nothing, since the firm alone is liable for all acts
Only the acts they personally sign, with no collective liability whatsoever
Only acts committed within the National Capital Region
n: Section 37(c) provides that "individual members of such firm, partnership association or corporation shall be responsible for their individual and collective acts as an entity and as provided by law." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37(c))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 3(6), an "Architectural Firm" may take which of the following forms, provided it is registered with the proper government agencies?
o: Only a corporation
A sole proprietorship, a partnership, or a corporation
Only a sole proprietorship
Only a cooperative
n: Section 3(6) defines "Architectural Firm" as "a sole proprietorship, a partnership or a corporation registered with the proper government agencies." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(6))

q: Under Section 13(a) of RA 9266, an applicant for the architecture licensure examination must establish to the Board's satisfaction that he/she is:
o: A resident of the province where the examination is administered
Employed full-time by a licensed architectural firm
A member of the integrated professional organization for at least one year
A Filipino citizen or a citizen of a foreign country qualified to take the examination as provided in this Act
n: Section 13(a) requires the applicant to establish that "he/she is a Filipino citizen or a citizen of a foreign country qualified to take the examination as provided for in this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13(a))

q: Of the members of the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture first appointed under RA 9266, Section 6 staggers their initial terms as follows: the chairman for three (3) years, one member for two (2) years, and the remaining member for how long?
o: Six (6) months
One (1) year
Two (2) years, same as the second member
Four (4) years
n: Section 6 states that of the first Board appointed, "one (1) member shall be appointed and hold office as chairman for three (3) years, one (1) member for two (2) years, and one (1) member for one (1) year." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 6)

q: RA 9266 was enacted during which session of the Philippine Congress, and when was it approved?
o: The Twelfth Congress, Third Regular Session; approved March 17, 2004
The Twelfth Congress, First Regular Session; approved March 17, 2005
The Eleventh Congress, First Regular Session; approved January 1, 2003
The Thirteenth Congress, Second Regular Session; approved July 28, 2003
n: The Act was begun and held by the Twelfth Congress, Third Regular Session, in Metro Manila, and RA 9266 bears the date March 17, 2004 as its approval date, signed by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo. (Source: RA 9266, Preamble/Approval)

q: Under Section 7(d) of RA 9266, the Board has the power to do what with a Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card for the practice of architecture?
o: Only issue it, with no power to suspend, revoke, or reinstate it
Issue, suspend, revoke, or reinstate it
Sell it to qualified bidders at public auction
Delegate all such actions exclusively to the Commission
n: Section 7(d) empowers the Board to "issue, suspend, revoke, or reinstate the Certificate of Registration and the professional Identification Card for the practice of the architecture profession." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(d))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 36, may an unregistered person lawfully collect a fee for architectural services?
o: Yes, provided the fee is below a certain amount
It is unlawful for any unregistered person to collect a fee for architectural services, except as an employee collecting a fee as representative of a registered architect
No, not even a registered architect's employee may ever collect fees on his behalf
Yes, without restriction
n: Section 36 states "it shall be unlawful for any unregistered person to collect a fee for architectural services except as an employee collecting a fee as representative of a Registered Architect." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 36)

q: Under Section 23(c) of RA 9266, which act by a registrant is a ground for suspension or revocation of his Certificate of Registration?
o: Falsely impersonating a practitioner or former practitioner of like or different name, or practicing under an assumed, fictitious or corporate name other than his/her own
Attending continuing professional development seminars
Charging fees lower than other architects in the same city
Refusing to accept new clients during a given year
n: Section 23(c) lists as a ground for suspension or revocation that the registrant "has falsely impersonated a practitioner, or former practitioner of alike or different name or has practiced under an assumed, fictitious or corporate name other than that of the registered." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(c))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 6, the members of the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture hold office for a term of how many years, and may be reappointed for how much further service?
o: A term of four (4) years, reappointable indefinitely
A term of two (2) years, reappointable for one additional year
A term of five (5) years, not subject to reappointment
A term of three (3) years, reappointable for one full additional term of three (3) years
n: Section 6 provides members "shall hold office for a term of three (3) years ... Each member of the Board may be reappointed for one full term of three (3) years." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 6)

q: Under the Statement of Policy in RA 9266, through what means does the State intend to develop competent, virtuous, productive and well-rounded professional architects?
o: Through abolition of the licensure examination in favor of on-the-job assessment
Through inviolable, honest, effective and credible licensure examinations and regulatory measures, programs and activities
Through mandatory foreign training programs only
Through unlimited automatic reciprocity with all foreign architects
n: Section 2 declares that the State shall nurture competent architects "through inviolable, honest, effective and credible licensure examinations and through regulatory measures, programs and activities that foster their professional growth and development." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 2)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 3(3), the "General Practice of Architecture" includes planning, architectural designing, structural conceptualization, specifying, and:
o: Only the preparation of real estate appraisals
Exclusively teaching architecture in universities
Supervising and giving general administration and responsible direction to the erection, enlargement or alterations of buildings and building environments
Solely the sale of construction materials
n: Section 3(3) defines General Practice of Architecture to include "supervising and giving general administration and responsible direction to the erection, enlargement or alterations of buildings and building environments and architectural design in engineering structures or any part thereof." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(3))

q: Under Section 13(d) of RA 9266, an applicant for the licensure examination must establish that he/she:
o: Has taught architecture for at least two years
Has published at least one architectural design in a journal
Has passed a foreign licensure examination
Has not been convicted of any criminal offense involving moral turpitude
n: Section 13(d) requires the applicant to establish "that he/she has not been convicted of any criminal offensive involving moral turpitude." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13(d))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 4, the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture is composed of:
o: Five (5) members with no designated chairman
A chairman and two (2) members
A chairman and four (4) members
A chairman and six (6) regional members
n: Section 4 creates the Board "to be composed of a chairman and two (2) members appointed by the President of the Philippines." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 4)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 43, does the Act affect or prevent the practice of other legally recognized professions?
o: No — Section 43 expressly provides that the Act shall not be construed to affect or prevent the practice of any other legally recognized profession
The Act is silent on this point
Yes, but only with respect to civil engineering
Yes, it supersedes and absorbs all allied professions into architecture
n: Section 43 states "this Act shall not be construed to affect or prevent the practice of any other legally recognized profession." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 43)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 3(10), a "Service Agreement" is described as:
o: A government permit required before construction may begin
A duly notarized written contract or equivalent public instrument stipulating the scope of services and guaranteeing compensation for services rendered by a registered and licensed architect
A certificate issued by the Board upon passing the licensure examination
An informal verbal understanding between architect and client
n: Section 3(10) defines a "Service Agreement" as "a duly notarized written contract or equivalent public instrument stipulating the scope of services and guaranteeing compensation of such services to be rendered by an architect registered and licensed under this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(10))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 17, before entering upon the practice of the profession, all successful examination candidates are required to:
o: Take an oath of profession before a Board member, an authorized government official, or any person authorized by law to administer oaths
Pay an additional examination fee
Complete a one-year unpaid apprenticeship
Secure a clearance from the Department of Trade and Industry
n: Section 17 requires successful candidates "to take an oath of profession before any member of the Board, any government official authorized by the Commission or any person authorized by law to administer oaths, prior to entering upon the practice of the profession." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 17)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 38(a), one of the conditions for a foreign national to be granted a temporary/special permit to practice architecture in the Philippines is that:
o: He/she is a citizen or subject of a country which specifically permits Filipino professionals to practice within its territorial limits on the same basis as its own subjects or citizens
He/she has already practiced in the Philippines for at least ten years without a permit
He/she has passed the Philippine licensure examination in a prior year
He/she is sponsored personally by a member of the Board
n: Section 38(a) requires that the foreign national "is a citizen or subject of a country which specifically permits Filipino professionals to practice his/her profession within their territorial limits, on the same basis as the subjects or citizens of such foreign state or country." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38(a))

q: Under Section 38(d) of RA 9266, agencies, organizations or individuals who secure the services of a foreign professional authorized to practice in the Philippines are responsible for securing a special permit from which two government offices?
o: The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
The Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) and the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE)
The Department of Foreign Affairs and the Commission on Higher Education
The Bureau of Immigration and the Bureau of Internal Revenue
n: Section 38(d) provides that such agencies, organizations or individuals "shall be responsible for securing a special permit from the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) and the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) pursuant to PRC and DOLE rules." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38(d))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 14, the licensure examination for architects covers, but is not limited to, how many groups of subjects?
o: Four (4)
Six (6)
Three (3)
Two (2)
n: Section 14 lists four subject groups: (1) History and Theory of Architecture/Principles of Planning and Architectural Practice; (2) Structural Design, Building Materials, Architectural Specifications, Methods of Construction and Utilities; (3) Urban Design and Architectural Interiors; and (4) Architectural Design and Site Planning. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 23, an aggrieved action of the Board suspending or revoking a Certificate of Registration is subject to what recourse, whose decision on it is final?
o: Appeal to the Department of Trade and Industry
No recourse is available at all
Appeal directly to the Supreme Court
Appeal to the Commission
n: Section 23 provides "that such action of the Board shall be subject to appeal to the Commission whose decision shall be final." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23)

q: Per Section 3(2) of RA 9266, an "Architect" is a person who, among other things, holds what two documents issued by the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture and the Professional Regulation Commission?
o: A diploma and a transcript of records
A tax identification number and a barangay clearance
A business permit and a mayor's clearance
A Certificate of Registration and a Professional Identification Card
n: Section 3(2) defines an Architect as a person "registered and licensed under this Act with a Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card issued by the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture and the Professional Regulation Commission." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(2))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 3(4)(e), the scope of the practice of architecture explicitly includes the preparation of which set of documents?
o: Preparation of building insurance actuarial tables
Preparation of environmental compliance certificates and land titles
Preparation of corporate income tax returns for construction firms
Preparation of architectural plans, specifications, bill of materials, cost estimates, general conditions and bidding documents
n: Section 3(4)(e) includes within the scope of architecture practice "preparation of architectural plans, specifications, bill of materials, cost estimates, general conditions and bidding documents." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(e))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 3(12), "Continuing Professional Development" (CPD) is defined as:
o: A grading system used only for board members
A mandatory annual re-examination identical to the licensure examination
A one-time refresher seminar taken only before retirement
A sustaining and progressive learning process that maintains, enhances, or increases the knowledge and continuing ability of architects
n: Section 3(12) defines CPD as "a sustaining and progressive learning process that maintains, enhances, or increases the knowledge and continuing ability of architects." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(12))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 11, the Board is required to submit an annual report to the Commission covering what content?
o: Only the list of examinees who failed the licensure examination
A detailed account of its proceedings during the year and recommendations it may deem proper
A five-year strategic plan for architecture education
Only the Board's annual budget request
n: Section 11 requires the Board to submit an annual report "giving a detailed account of its proceedings during the year and making such recommendations as it may deem proper." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 11)

q: An examinee in the architecture licensure examination obtains the following subject grades: History/Theory 78%, Structural Design 68%, Urban Design/Interiors 74%, and Architectural Design/Site Planning 72%. Her weighted general average computes to 73%. Under RA 9266, Section 15, has she passed?
o: Yes, but only if she retakes the Structural Design subject
Yes, because her weighted general average of 73% is at least 70% and no single subject grade fell below 50%
No, because her Structural Design grade of 68% is below the 70% general average threshold
No, because a general average alone is never sufficient regardless of subject grades
n: Section 15 requires "a weighted general average of seventy percent (70%), with no grade lower than fifty percent (50%) in any given subject." Her 73% average meets the 70% threshold, and no subject grade is below 50%, so she passes. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 15)
scenario: A candidate for the architecture licensure examination receives the following subject ratings: History and Theory of Architecture — 78%; Structural Design, Building Materials, Specifications, Construction and Utilities — 68%; Urban Design and Architectural Interiors — 74%; Architectural Design and Site Planning — 72%. Her computed weighted general average is 73%.

q: An architect signs plans that were actually made under another architect's supervision, without indicating which parts he/she actually performed. Under Section 20(3) of RA 9266, is this lawful?
o: Yes, signing another architect's work is always permitted between colleagues
No, but only if the plans are for a government project
Yes, as long as the supervising architect gives verbal permission

No — Section 20(3) makes it unlawful to sign or seal such plans unless done in a manner that clearly indicates the parts of the work actually performed by the signer, and unlawful for any person except the architect-of-record to sign for work not actually performed by him/her
n: Section 20(3) provides it is unlawful for an architect to sign or affix a seal on plans made under another architect's supervision "unless the same is made in such manner as to clearly indicate the part or parts of such work actually performed by the former," and unlawful for any person except the architect-of-record to sign for work not actually performed. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(3))

q: Under Section 7(f) of RA 9266, the Board is empowered to monitor conditions affecting the practice of architecture and to do what?
o: Certify building structural safety in place of licensed engineers
Adopt such measures as may be deemed proper for the enhancement and maintenance of high professional, ethical and technical standards of the profession
Set construction material prices nationwide
Directly prosecute criminal cases in court without the Commission
n: Section 7(f) empowers the Board to "monitor the conditions affecting the practice of architecture and adopt such measures as may be deemed proper for the enhancement and maintenance of high professional, ethical and technical standards of the profession." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(f))

q: Under Section 7(b) of RA 9266, one of the Board's specific powers and functions is to:
o: Elect the President of the integrated professional organization
Supervise the registration, licensure and practice of architects
Approve building permits issued by local government units
Set the national budget for infrastructure spending
n: Section 7(b) empowers the Board to "supervise the registration, licensure and practice of architects." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(b))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 3(7), the term "Authorship" refers to the author or authors of a set of architectural plans or specifications who are in charge of their preparation, whether made:
o: Exclusively by a computer-aided design program
By any unlicensed drafter regardless of supervision
By the client's in-house engineering staff only
By them personally or under their immediate supervision
n: Section 3(7) defines "Authorship" as referring to those in charge of preparing the plans or specifications, "whether made by them personally or under their immediate supervision." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(7))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 7(h), an administrative case decision of the Board, unless appealed to the Commission, becomes final and executory after how many days from receipt of notice of the judgment or decision?
o: Ten (10) days
Thirty (30) days
Fifteen (15) days
Sixty (60) days
n: Section 7(h) provides "the decision of the Board shall, unless appealed to the Commission, become final and executory after fifteen (15) days from receipt of notice of judgment or decision." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(h))

q: What is the short title of Republic Act No. 9266?
o: The Architects' Code of the Philippines
The Professional Architects Act
The Architecture Act of 2004
The Philippine Architecture Regulation Act
n: Section 1 of RA 9266 states: "This Act shall be known as 'The Architecture Act of 2004.'" (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 1)

q: An architect signs and affixes his seal on architectural plans that were not actually prepared by him/her nor executed under his/her immediate supervision. Under Section 23(a) of RA 9266, what is the consequence?
o: It is only a civil matter between the architect and the client
It is a ground for the Board to suspend or revoke his Certificate of Registration/Professional Identification Card, subject to appeal to the Commission
It automatically results in permanent disbarment with no right of appeal
No consequence, as long as the plans are structurally sound
n: Section 23(a) makes it a ground for suspension or revocation where the architect "has signed and affixed or permitted to be signed or affixed his name or seal on architectural plans and designs, specification, drawings, technical reports, valuation, estimates, or other similar documents or work not prepared by him/her or not executed under his/her immediate supervision," subject to appeal to the Commission. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(a))

q: Section 7(e) of RA 9266 grants the Board which specific power?
o: Print its own currency for examination fees
Adopt an official seal of the Board
Grant honorary architecture degrees
Appoint judges to the Court of Appeals
n: Section 7(e) empowers the Board to "adopt an official seal of the Board." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(e))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 28, aside from the integrated and accredited professional organization developing a CPD program for architects, who else may become CPD providers?
o: Only foreign universities
No other entity may ever provide CPD
Only the Commission itself
Other entities or organizations, upon accreditation by the Board
n: Section 28 provides "other entities or organizations may become CPD providers upon accreditation by the Board." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 28)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 29 (Prohibition in the Practice of Architecture and Penal Clause), a person convicted of practicing architecture without being registered/licensed shall, upon conviction, be sentenced to a fine within what range?
o: Not less than Ten thousand pesos (P10,000.00) but not more than One hundred thousand pesos (P100,000.00)
A flat fine of exactly Fifty thousand pesos (P50,000.00) with no range
Not less than Five hundred thousand pesos (P500,000.00) but not more than Ten million pesos (P10,000,000.00)
Not less than One hundred thousand pesos (P100,000.00) but not more than Five million pesos (P5,000,000.00)
n: Section 29 imposes "a fine of not less than One hundred thousand pesos (P100,000.00) but not more than Five Million pesos (P5,000,000.00) or...imprisonment for a period not less than six (6) months or not exceeding six (6) years, or both, at the discretion of the Court." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29)

q: A Board member is shown to have tolerated a violation of the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice by a registrant. Under Section 9(b) of RA 9266, is this a valid ground for suspension or removal of that Board member?
o: Yes — violation or tolerance of a violation of the Act, its IRR, or the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice is an express ground under Section 9(b)
No, only the registrant who committed the violation may be penalized
Yes, but only if the tolerance is repeated at least three times
No, tolerance of a violation by another person cannot be attributed to a Board member
n: Section 9(b) lists as a ground for suspension or removal "violation of tolerance of the violation of this Act, or its implementing rules and regulations or the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 9(b))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 47 (Effectivity), the Act takes effect how many days following its publication in the Official Gazette or in two newspapers of general circulation?
o: Fifteen (15) days
Thirty (30) days
Sixty (60) days
Ten (10) days
n: Section 47 states "this Act shall take effect after fifteen 15 (5) days following its publication in the Official Gazette or in two (2) newspapers of general circulation" — the operative period is fifteen (15) days. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 47)

q: Under Section 3(4)(j) of RA 9266, the scope of the practice of architecture also includes "all other works, projects and activities which require the professional competence of an architect," expressly naming which two examples?
o: Teaching of architectural subjects and architectural computer-aided design
Managing hospital operations and running clinical trials
Practicing law and accounting
Conducting geological surveys and mineral exploration
n: Section 3(4)(j) covers "all other works, projects and activities which require the professional competence of an architect, including teaching of architectural subjects and architectural computer-aided design." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(j))

q: Which of the following is listed as a power and function of the Board under Section 7(c) of RA 9266?
o: Deputize the Philippine National Police for enforcement
Administer oaths in connection with the administration of this Act
Impose real property taxes on architectural firms
Appoint the Secretary of the Department of Trade and Industry
n: Section 7(c) grants the Board power to "administer oaths in connection with the administration of this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(c))

q: An architect openly solicits and undertakes architectural work for a client without first executing a valid service agreement guaranteeing compensation. Under RA 9266, Section 23(e), what may the Board do?
o: Suspend or revoke the architect's Certificate of Registration/Professional Identification Card, since openly soliciting or undertaking services without a valid service agreement is a ground for suspension or revocation
Only impose a verbal warning with no further consequence
Refer the matter exclusively to the Department of Trade and Industry
Nothing, since a service agreement is merely optional under the Act
n: Section 23(e) lists as a ground for suspension or revocation having "openly solicited projects by actually undertaking architectural services without a valid service agreement guaranteeing compensation of services to be rendered." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(e))

q: Under Section 23(f) of RA 9266, which broad catch-all ground supports suspension or revocation of a Certificate of Registration?
o: Having practiced architecture for more than twenty-five years
Having declined a project on grounds of conflict of interest
Having violated any provision of this Act, its implementing rules and regulations, or the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice
Having designed a building that later required renovation
n: Section 23(f) lists as a ground for suspension or revocation that the registrant "has violated any provision of this Act, its implementing rules and regulations, the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(f))

q: Under Section 13(b) of RA 9266, in addition to citizenship, what personal qualification must an examination applicant establish?
o: That he/she is of good moral character
That he/she has passed a separate government aptitude test
That he/she is at least 30 years of age
That he/she has no outstanding student loans
n: Section 13(b) requires the applicant to establish "that he/she is of good moral character." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13(b))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 34, a person who is not a registered architect is prohibited from doing what, even if no form of the title "Architect" is actually used?
o: Selling construction materials to licensed architects
Claiming or representing their services or work as equivalent to those of a duly qualified registered architect, or that they are qualified for any branch or function of architectural practice
Working in a construction site in any capacity whatsoever
Attending architecture-related seminars
n: Section 34 provides that non-registered persons "shall not claim nor represent either services or work as equivalent to those of a duly qualified registered architect, or that they are qualified for any branch or functions of function of architectural practice, even though no form of the title 'Architect' is used." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 34)

q: Section 3(4)(g) of RA 9266 includes which of the following within the scope of the practice of architecture?
o: Structural conceptualization of engineering works only
Issuing business permits for architectural firms
Conducting the licensure examination for architects

The planning, architectural lay-outing and utilization of spaces within and surrounding buildings, including housing design, community architecture, architectural interiors, space planning, detailing, lighting, acoustics, and lay-outing of mechanical, electrical, electronic, sanitary, plumbing, communications and other utility systems
n: Section 3(4)(g) covers "the planning, architectural lay-outing and utilization of spaces within and surrounding such buildings or structures, housing design and community architecture, architectural interiors and space planning, architectural detailing, architectural lighting, acoustics, architectural lay-outing of mechanical, electrical, electronic, sanitary, plumbing, communications and other utility systems, equipment and fixtures." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(g))

q: What is the full descriptive title given to RA 9266 in its enacting clause, describing its overall purpose?
o: An Act establishing minimum wage standards for licensed architects
An Act creating the Department of Architecture of the Philippines
An Act abolishing the licensure examination for architects
An Act providing for a more responsive and comprehensive regulation for the registration, licensing and practice of architecture, repealing Republic Act No. 545, as amended, and for other purposes
n: RA 9266's full title describes it as "AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MORE RESPONSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE REGULATION FOR THE REGISTRATION, LICENSING AND PRACTICE OF ARCHITECTURE, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 545, AS AMENDED...AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES." (Source: RA 9266, Title/Enacting Clause)

q: Using the same candidate's ratings above, suppose her Structural Design grade had instead been 48% while her weighted general average still computed to 71%. Under RA 9266, Section 15, would she pass the licensure examination?
o: No — even though her general average of 71% exceeds 70%, a subject grade of 48% is below the 50% minimum required in any given subject, so she fails
No, because the general average must be at least 75% regardless of subject grades
Yes, because only the general average matters under the Act, not individual subject grades
Yes, because her 71% weighted general average exceeds the 70% minimum
n: Section 15 requires both a 70% weighted general average AND no grade lower than 50% in any given subject; a 48% subject grade fails that second condition regardless of the overall average. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 15)
scenario: A candidate for the architecture licensure examination receives the following subject ratings: History and Theory of Architecture — 78%; Structural Design, Building Materials, Specifications, Construction and Utilities — 68%; Urban Design and Architectural Interiors — 74%; Architectural Design and Site Planning — 72%. Her computed weighted general average is 73%.

q: Under RA 9266, Section 14, "Urban Design and Architectural Interiors" is grouped as a licensure examination subject together with what other topic in the same numbered subject group?
o: It is grouped with Architectural Design and Site Planning as one combined subject
It is grouped with History and Theory of Architecture
It is grouped with Structural Design and Building Materials
It stands as its own separate subject group, item (3)
n: Section 14(3) lists "Urban Design and Architectural Interiors" as its own subject grouping, distinct from item (4) "Architectural Design and Site Planning." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14(3))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 3(5), "Structural Conceptualization" is defined as the act of conceiving, choosing and developing the type, disposition, arrangement and proportioning of the structural elements of an architectural work with due consideration to:
o: Only the aesthetic appeal of the facade
Only compliance with foreign building codes
Only the lowest possible material cost regardless of safety
Safety, cost-effectiveness, functionality and aesthetics
n: Section 3(5) defines Structural Conceptualization as giving due consideration to "safety, cost-effectiveness, functionality and aesthetics." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(5))

q: Which of the following is expressly named among the powers and functions of the Board under RA 9266, Section 7(m)?
o: Fixing the retail price of construction materials
Adopting a program for the full computerization of the licensure examination
Setting the national minimum wage for architects
Issuing business permits for architectural firms
n: Section 7(m) empowers the Board "to adopt a program for the full computerization of the licensure examination." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(m))

q: An unlicensed contractor knowingly allows the use and implementation of architectural plans prepared by a firm not duly licensed to practice architecture. Under RA 9266, Section 29, is this conduct covered by the penal clause?
o: Yes — Section 29 also penalizes any person who knowingly allows the use, adoption or implementation of plans, designs or specifications made by a person, firm, partnership or company not duly licensed to practice architecture
Yes, but only if the contractor is a foreigner
No, Section 29 covers only the unlicensed person who drew the plans, not those who merely use them
No, this is addressed only under the National Building Code, not RA 9266
n: Section 29 penalizes "any person whether Filipino or foreigner, who knowingly allows the use, adoption, implementation of plans, designs or specification made by any person, firm, partnership or company not duly licensed to engage in the practice of architecture." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 44, whose primary duty is it to effectively enforce the provisions of the Act, with assistance from duly constituted law enforcement agencies upon call or request?
o: The local barangay captains alone
The Securities and Exchange Commission alone
The Department of Trade and Industry alone
The Commission and the Board
n: Section 44 states "it shall be the primary duty of the Commission and the Board to effectively enforce the provision of this Act," with law enforcement agencies rendering assistance upon call or request. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 44)

q: In RA 9266, Section 3(13) and (14), the abbreviations "DTI" and "SEC" stand for:
o: Department of Trade and Industry; Securities and Exchange Commission
Department of Tourism and Investment; Society of Engineers and Contractors
Department of Technical Instruction; Standards Enforcement Commission
Design and Technology Institute; Secretariat of Education and Commerce
n: Section 3(13) provides "DTI" shall mean the Department of Trade and Industry, and Section 3(14) provides "SEC" shall mean the Securities and Exchange Commission. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(13)-(14))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 20(2), a city or municipal officer charged with enforcing building construction laws shall not accept, approve, or approve payment for architectural plans that were not:
o: Prepared and submitted in full accord with all the provisions of this Act, and signed and sealed by the author
Printed on government-issued paper
Translated into English
Notarized by a lawyer
n: Section 20(2) prohibits government officers from accepting or approving plans "which have not been prepared and submitted in full accord with all the provisions of this Act," or approving payment for work not "signed and sealed by the author." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(2))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 21, aside from the Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card and their dates, what additional number must an architect indicate on documents signed, used or issued in connection with the practice of the profession?
o: The architect's voter's identification number
The professional tax receipt (PTR) number
The architect's personal Social Security System (SSS) number
The architect's home telephone number
n: Section 21 requires an architect to indicate the Certificate of Registration and PIC details "including the professional tax receipt number, on the documents he/she signs, uses or issues." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 21)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 10, the compensation and allowances of the chairman and members of the Board shall be:
o: Comparable to that received by the chairman and members of existing regulatory boards under the Commission, as provided in the General Appropriations Act
Limited to per diem allowances only, with no salary
Paid directly by the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects
Fixed permanently at the rate set in 2004 with no future adjustment
n: Section 10 provides Board compensation "comparable to that being received by the chairman and members of existing regulatory Boards under the Commission as provided for in the General Appropriations Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 10)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 3(8) and (9), what do the terms "Board" and "Commission" respectively refer to?
o: "Board" refers to the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization
"Board" refers to the Professional Regulation Commission; "Commission" refers to the Board of Architecture
"Board" refers to the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture; "Commission" refers to the Professional Regulation Commission
Both terms refer interchangeably to the Department of Trade and Industry
n: Section 3(8) provides that "Board" refers to the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture, while Section 3(9) provides that "Commission" means the Professional Regulation Commission. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(8)-(9))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 42, the funding for implementing the Act shall be included by the Chairperson of the Professional Regulation Commission in what document?
o: The Board's private trust fund
The integrated professional organization's membership dues schedule
The annual General Appropriations Act
A special foreign grant application
n: Section 42 provides that the Chairperson of the Commission shall include implementation of the Act in Commission programs, "the funding of which shall be included in the annual General Appropriations Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 42)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 19, the Board is required to prepare and update a roster showing:
o: Only architects who failed the licensure examination
Only the names of foreign architects holding temporary permits
Only the names of Board members over the years
The names and place of business of all registered professional architects, made available to any party as may be deemed necessary
n: Section 19 requires "a roster showing the names and place of business of all registered professional architects...prepared and updated by the Board and copies thereof shall be made available to any party as may be deemed necessary." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 19)

q: A Board member is found to have disclosed secret and confidential examination questions before the licensure examination was conducted. Under RA 9266, Section 9, is this a valid ground for the President, upon recommendation of the Commission, to suspend or remove that member?
o: No, disclosure of exam questions is only an internal disciplinary matter with no removal consequence
No, only criminal conviction is a valid ground for removal
Yes, but only if the disclosure is proven in a criminal court first
Yes — Section 9(d) names manipulation or rigging of examination results and disclosure of secret and confidential examination information as a ground for suspension or removal
n: Section 9(d) lists as a ground for suspension or removal "manipulation or rigging of the architecture licensure examination results, disclosure of secret and confidential information in the examination questions prior to the conduct of the said examination or tampering of grades." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 9(d))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 25, no person shall practice architecture, prepare architectural plans for buildings in the country, or use the title "Architect" unless that person has received from the Board:
o: A diploma in architecture from any recognized school
A business permit from the local government unit only
A Certificate of Registration and a Professional Identification Card, in the manner provided by the Act
Membership in a private professional club
n: Section 25 requires that a person "shall have received from the Board a Certificate of Registration and be issued a Professional Identification Card in the manner hereinafter provided" before practicing architecture or using the title "Architect." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 25)

q: A group of professionals wishes to form and register a firm for the practice of architecture in the Philippines. Under RA 9266, Section 37(a), who may, among themselves or together with allied technical professionals, form and obtain such registration?
o: Any foreign national residing in the Philippines
Only Filipino citizens properly registered and licensed as architects under this Act
Only civil engineers, without any architect involvement
Any corporation, regardless of the profession of its incorporators
n: Section 37(a) provides "only Filipino citizens properly registered and licensed as architects under this Act may, among themselves, or together with allied technical professionals, form and obtain registration as a firm, company, partnership, association or corporation for the practice of architecture." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37(a))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 20(4), drawings and specifications duly signed, stamped or sealed are treated as instruments of service and are considered:
o: The exclusive property of the contractor who built the project
Public domain material free for anyone to copy
Government property once a building permit is issued
The intellectual properties and documents of the architect, whether or not the object for which they were made is executed
n: Section 20(4) states such drawings "are the intellectual properties and documents of the architect, whether the object for which they are made is executed or not," and prohibits unauthorized duplication or copying. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(4))

q: A newly-organized Board wants to require all licensed architects to attend CPD seminars as a precondition for renewing their professional license. Under RA 9266, Section 7(i), may the Board impose this as a mandatory renewal requirement?
o: Yes, but only for architects below 40 years of age
Yes, CPD attendance is an absolute prerequisite for license renewal under the Act
No, because the Board has no authority over CPD at all
No — Section 7(i) expressly provides that CPD attendance shall not be a mandatory requirement for the renewal of a professional license
n: Section 7(i) authorizes the Board to prescribe CPD guidelines but expressly provides "that the attendance to said CPD shall not be a mandatory requirement for the renewal of a professional license." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(i))

q: A licensed architect's Certificate of Registration expired six months ago and was never renewed. Under RA 9266, Section 20(1), may this architect continue to lawfully stamp or seal architectural documents with the official seal issued to him?
o: No — it is unlawful to stamp or seal any documents with the seal after the certificate has expired or been revoked, unless the certificate has been renewed or re-issued
Yes, the seal remains valid indefinitely once issued
