No, but only if a client formally complains to the Board
Yes, as long as he pays a late renewal penalty after the fact
n: Section 20(1) makes it "unlawful for any one to stamp or seal any documents with said seal after the certificate of the registrant named thereon has expired or has been revoked, unless said certificate shall have been renewed or re-issued." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(1))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 5(c), a nominee to the Board must have been an active practitioner of architecture, holding a valid Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card, for at least how many years on the date of appointment?
o: Five (5) years
Ten (10) years
Fifteen (15) years
Seven (7) years
n: Section 5(c) requires a Board member to "be an architect with a valid Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card and active practitioner of architecture for at least ten (10) years on the date of his/her appointment." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 5(c))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 4, within how many months from the effectivity of the Act must the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture be organized?
o: Six (6) months
One (1) year
Two (2) years
Three (3) months
n: Section 4 states: "The Board shall be organized not later than six (6) months from the effectivity of this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 4)

q: Under RA 9266, Section 27, a non-Filipino citizen applying to take the licensure examination must prove that his or her own country, by specific provision of law, does what with respect to Filipino architects?
o: Requires Filipino architects to pay a special foreign tax before practicing
Prohibits Filipino architects from ever practicing there

Admits Filipino citizens to the same profession without restriction, or allows them to practice after examination on terms of strict and absolute equality, including unconditional recognition of Philippine degrees
Automatically grants a Philippine license without any examination
n: Section 27's reciprocity requirement obliges the foreign applicant to prove his country "admits citizens of the Philippines to the practice of the same profession without restriction or allows them to practice it after passing an examination on terms of strict and absolute equality...including the unconditional recognition of prerequisite degrees/diplomas." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 27)

q: Under Section 14(4) of RA 9266, which subject rounds out the four listed examination subjects for architects?
o: Building Code Enforcement and Zoning Law
Interior Design and Furniture Fabrication
Architectural Design and Site Planning
Quantity Surveying and Cost Estimation
n: Section 14(4) lists "Architectural Design and Site Planning" as one of the subjects for the licensure examination. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14(4))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 24, in reinstating a revoked Certificate of Registration, may the Board exempt the applicant from taking another licensure examination?
o: Yes — the Board may, in its discretion, exempt the applicant from taking another examination
Only foreign architects may be granted such exemption
No, a new examination is always mandatory for reinstatement
Only the Commission, never the Board, may grant such exemption
n: Section 24 states the Board "may, in its discretion, exempt the applicant from taking another examination" when reinstating a revoked Certificate of Registration. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 24)

q: An architectural corporation has 100 total owners/shareholders/incorporators/directors/executive officers. Under RA 9266, Section 37(b), what is the minimum number of these persons who must be registered and licensed architects for the firm to lawfully register for the practice of architecture?
o: At least 25 (25%)
At least 75 (75%)
At least 50 (50%)
n: Section 37(b) requires that "registered and licensed architects shall compose at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the owners, shareholders, members, incorporators, directors, executive officers, as the case may be." Seventy-five percent of 100 is 75. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37(b))
scenario: An architectural firm organizing as a corporation will have a total of 100 persons counted among its owners, shareholders, incorporators, directors and executive officers combined.

q: Under RA 9266, Section 7(a) and (g), the Board's powers and functions include:
o: Prescribing and adopting rules and regulations to carry out this Act, and prescribing/adopting the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice
Only hearing criminal cases filed in regular courts
Setting foreign exchange rates for imported architectural materials
Only administering the licensure examination, with no rule-making authority whatsoever
n: Section 7(a) empowers the Board to "prescribe and adopt the rules and regulations necessary for carrying out the provisions of this Act," and Section 7(g) to "prescribe and/or adopt the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(a), (g))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 3(1), how is "Architecture" defined?
o: The trade of assembling prefabricated building components
The exclusive act of preparing structural computations for buildings
The business of managing real estate development projects

The art, science or profession of planning, designing and constructing buildings in their totality, taking into account their environment, in accordance with the principles of utility, strength and beauty
n: Section 3(1) defines Architecture as "the art, science or profession of planning, designing and constructing buildings in their totality taking into account their environment, in accordance with the principles of utility, strength and beauty." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(1))

q: Under Section 5(a) of RA 9266, one of the qualifications a person must possess at the time of appointment as a member of the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture is that he/she must be:
o: A citizen and resident of the Philippines
A holder of a law degree in addition to architecture
A resident of Metro Manila for at least twenty (20) years
A member of the House of Representatives
n: Section 5(a) requires each Board member to "be a citizen and resident of the Philippines." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 5(a))

q: Under Section 7(j) of RA 9266, in relation to the licensure examination, the Board is empowered to prepare, adopt, issue or amend the syllabi of examination subjects and to do what else?
o: Determine and prepare questions within the scope of the syllabi, and administer, correct and release the results of the licensure examinations
Set examination fees without limit or approval
Waive the examination for foreign-trained applicants automatically
Delegate the entire examination process to private review centers
n: Section 7(j) empowers the Board to "prepare, adopt, issue or amend the syllabi of the subjects for examinations by determining and preparing questions...as well as administer, correct and release the results of the licensure examinations." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(j))

q: An architect with exceptional or recognized expertise or specialization in a particular branch of architecture, engaged for that specialized expertise, is termed under RA 9266 as a:
o: Integrated architect
Architecture-in-charge of construction
Architect-of-record
Consulting Architect
n: Section 3(2)(c) defines "Consulting Architect" as an architect "with exceptional or recognized expertise or specialization in any branch of architecture." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(2)(c))

q: Under Section 7(n) of RA 9266, the Board's catch-all power allows it to discharge such other duties and functions deemed necessary for what purpose?
o: The transfer of Board functions to local government units
The abolition of the integrated professional organization
The enhancement of the architecture profession and the upgrading, development and growth of architecture education
The privatization of the licensure examination process
n: Section 7(n) empowers the Board to "discharge such other duties and functions as may be deemed necessary for the enhancement of the architecture profession and the upgrading, development and growth of the architecture education." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(n))

q: Under Section 3(4)(f) of RA 9266, the Scope of the Practice of Architecture expressly includes "construction and project management," covering general management, administration, supervision, coordination and responsible direction of which activities?
o: Only the hiring and payroll of construction laborers
Only the financing and loan processing for the project
Only the marketing and advertising of the finished building

Planning, architectural designing, construction, reconstruction, erection, enlargement or demolition, renovation, repair, remodeling, alteration, preservation or restoration of buildings or structures
n: Section 3(4)(f) lists "construction and project management, giving general management, administration, supervision, coordination and responsible direction or the planning, architectural designing, construction, reconstruction, erection, enlargement or demolition, renovation, repair, orderly removal, remodeling, alteration, preservation or restoration of buildings or structures" as part of the scope of practice. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(f))

q: Under RA 9266, Section 37(d), a firm, partnership, association or corporation practicing architecture must be registered with which two entities?
o: The integrated and accredited professional organization only
The Bureau of Internal Revenue and the Commission on Higher Education
The Department of Trade and Industry and the local government unit
The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Board
n: Section 37(d) requires "such firm, partnership, association or corporation shall be registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission and Board." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37(d))

q: An architect's Certificate of Registration was revoked. Under RA 9266, Section 24, after how many years from the date of revocation may the Board, upon application and for reasons deemed proper and sufficient, reinstate the validity of the revoked certificate?
o: Two (2) years
Three (3) years
Five (5) years
One (1) year
n: Section 24 provides the Board may act "after the expiration of two (2) years from the date of revocation of a Certificate of Registration, Professional Identification Card or special/temporary permit." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 24)
